briefs: docs/round10/track-w.md (read W0 first: its rules 1 to 4 and the call sites; W2 and W3 for the game event helpers and the frequency table), docs/round10/decisions.md (the entry 'W's merge kept both sides and added the vibrations W's brief leaves to the second merger', which lists the sites this segment covers) and docs/round10/track-w-log.md (what w1 and w2 built)
notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: D0 (shared mob registry), E2 (known limits), M1 (land animals), M3 (night mobs), later M2 (water mobs). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small. Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. SEGMENT w3: the game events that W's w1 merge left out because other tracks built their sites. W's helpers exist (Level::game_event, EntityWorld::game_event, Entities::game_event, the frequency and radius table in minecraft_terrain's vibrations.rs). Follow W0 rule 1: one line per call site, placed after the state change it reports, no call site restructured. Before adding a line, find the vanilla 26.3 call with javap on the 26.3 jar (event id, source entity, position, affected block state) and write it in the track log; where vanilla posts no event, add none and say so in the log. Each event gets a test in the crate that owns its site (the event queued with the right id, position and source), and the sculk sensor frequency from the table is checked where the brief's W2 tests do that. The owner's test steps use a sculk sensor with a comparator into a line of redstone dust, like W3's steps, and give the line's length for each source. Merges since the briefs: D (trial spawners, vaults, lodestones, breezes), D0's d0a and d0b (the registry, silverfish hiding in and waking from infested blocks, endermites from ender pearls, flying navigation), E1, E2 (thrown things, doors broken by mobs, lead knots, cats on chests, fireworks, maps), F (Margit), W's w1 and w2 (wardens) and M1's first segments are all in minecraft-survival; the orchestrator merges minecraft-survival into track-w before this run, so the review uses git diff r10-w3-base..HEAD as usual.

groups.prompt: Track W group events-items (segment w3): the game events of things E2 and D built in round 10. One commit, 'Minecraft lead knots, firework rockets and the ominous item spawner post their game events': lead knots (tying a mob to a fence, punching a knot off, shearing a lead; find E2's lead knot code with git log --grep 'lead' and the vanilla calls in LeadItem, LeashFenceKnotEntity and Leashable), firework rockets as projectiles (launched by a player, a crossbow or a dispenser, and hitting a block or a mob; the burst's explode line exists since the w1 merge, check it still sits after the burst), and the ominous item spawner of ominous trial spawners (D's d1; vanilla OminousItemSpawner). Keep each to one line per site through the existing helpers.

Track W group events-mobs (segment w3): the game events of mobs at blocks and of mob equipment. One commit, 'Minecraft silverfish, villagers and piglins at doors and mob equipment post their game events': silverfish breaking out of infested blocks and hiding in stone (D0's d0b, third_party/minecraftoss/entities/src/world/families/pests/silverfish.rs and its level side; vanilla SilverfishWakeUpFriendsGoal, SilverfishMergeWithStoneGoal and Level.destroyBlock), villagers and piglins opening and closing doors (vanilla InteractWithDoor through DoorBlock.setOpen with the mob as source; find the fork's villager and piglin door code), and mobs putting on and taking off equipment (vanilla LivingEntity.onEquipItem posts equip or unequip; find where the fork's mobs pick up or are given armour and held items: zombies, skeletons, piglins, villagers, foxes if M1 has merged them). If one of these has no site in the fork yet, say so in the log and leave it.
